notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text identifies When Your World Must Be Defended: Choosing Products to Justify the System; all five authors match Cutright, Wu, Banfield, Kay, and Fitzsimons. Journal of Consumer Research 38(1), June 2011, pp. 62–77 and DOI 10.1086/658469 match the original reference. The text contains the primary published article, methods/results for five experiments and references, rather than an abstract or secondary report. Source header names a Wharton-hosted publication PDF. No PDF path was supplied; no network acquisition or PDF rendering performed. Target assessment: study_o and description are null, and the only original locator is p. 13. Counting the supplied cover gives page 13 = printed p. 73; counting from the article title page gives article page 13 = printed p. 74. Both contain multiple tests. The replication reference project token eg3p does not independently identify an original outcome/sample/test and cannot resolve this locator. No target selected using numeric agreement or input order. Candidates on printed p. 73 (Experiment 4): direct-outcome condition × confidence interaction B = −1.37, t(1,84) = −3.89, p = .0002; indirect brand-choice simple condition effect at low confidence B = −1.09, t(1,84) = −2.92, p = .004; indirect effect at high confidence B = .28, t(1,84) = .94, p = .35; direct derogation effect at low confidence B = 1.14, t(1,84) = 1.66, p = .10; direct effect at high confidence B = −2.37, t(1,84) = −4.25, p < .0001. These are distinct same-test coefficient/p pairs; none assigned to this row. Printed p. 72 additionally reports the Experiment 4 omnibus F(1,84) = 20.68, p < .0001 and indirect interaction B = .54, t(1,84) = 2.80, p = .01. Candidates on printed p. 74 (Experiment 5): three-way logistic interaction B = −1.29, Z = −3.15, p < .01; indirect-brand interaction B = .50, Z = 2.03, p = .04; direct-brand interaction B = −.79, Z = 2.41, p = .02; indirect low-confidence effect B = −1.01, Z = −1.98, p = .05; indirect high-confidence effect B = .22, Z = .61, p = .54; direct low-confidence effect B = .38, Z = .81, p = .42; direct high-confidence effect B = −1.58, Z = −2.32, p < .02. Pretest t(27) = 10.40, p < .0001 is a different sample/test. Printed B coefficients are not ORs; no exponentiation or other conversion performed. N candidates: Experiment 4 has 88 recruited participants (printed p. 71), Experiment 5 has 138 recruited participants (printed p. 73), and its pretest has 28 adults (printed p. 74). Recruitment counts are not promoted to target analytic N. Experiment 3 explicitly states 83 participants included after reaction-latency/error exclusions (printed p. 70), but that different experiment cannot be assigned from the sparse locator. No N derived from df or summed. All three assigned fields remain unresolved because the outcome/test and study correspondence are ambiguous. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders only; no replication source examined.
